As an installation artist, I build pieces that occupy a room rather than hang on its wall. Topiary, robotics, kinetic sculpture, and projected light, assembled into one thing an audience can walk around.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4" css=".vc_custom_oddtoe_col_gutter{padding-left: 20px;padding-right: 20px;}"][vc_column_text]The work is site-specific. A gallery, a hotel foyer, a laneway, a festival field, and a shopping centre atrium all want different objects, so the design starts with the space and the route people take through it. I design in 3D first, then work with fabricators to get the piece built and installed. screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4" css=".vc_custom_oddtoe_col_gutter{padding-left: 20px;padding-right: 20px;}"][vc_column_text css=""]Installation art is three-dimensional work made for a particular space, where the room, the route through it, and the audience are all part of the piece. A painting works on any wall. An installation is designed around its site, its lighting, and the way people move past it.

The term covers a lot of ground. It can be one large object under a spotlight, a whole room the audience walks into, or a set of pieces spread across a park.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4" css=".vc_custom_oddtoe_col_gutter{padding-left: 20px;padding-right: 20px;}"][vc_column_text css=""]What those have in common is that the location is not a backdrop. Move the work somewhere else and it becomes a different work.

Oddtoe treats that as the interesting part of the job. If a viewer has to walk around something, then their path, their eye line, and what they see when they turn around are all things to design. Closely related practices — kinetic sculpture and projection art — often end up inside the same commission.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="default_row_small_paddings" dfd_row_responsive_enable="dfd-row-responsive-enable" responsive_styles="padding_left_mobile:10|padding_right_mobile:10"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="60" screen_tablet_spacer_size="50" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_family:BebasNeueRegular|letter_spacing:0" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_family:QwigleyRegular" subtitle="Living material, metal, machinery, and light" heading_margin="margin-bottom:10px;"]What Goes Into an Oddtoe Installation?[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4" css=".vc_custom_oddtoe_col_gutter{padding-left: 20px;padding-right: 20px;}"][vc_column_text css=""]Topiary, robotics, kinetic sculpture, projected light, and generative-AI animation. Most Oddtoe installations combine several of these in one piece — a planted form with a moving mechanical element, projected onto after dark. Materials I've used (and wish to use) include living plants, sheet metal, resin, and fired clay.

Each of those is a practice in its own right, and each has its own page:[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4" css=".vc_custom_oddtoe_col_gutter{padding-left: 20px;padding-right: 20px;}"][vc_column_text css=""]• Topiary and planted forms
• Kinetic sculpture
• Robotics and animatronics
• Projection and light
• Props and fabricated objects
• Sensory garden design
• Giant inflatables and walk-in structures

The newer ingredient is generative AI, used for concept exploration and for the animated content that gets projected onto a built piece. There is a full explainer on what generative AI animation is.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_responsive_enable="dfd-row-responsive-enable" responsive_styles="padding_left_mobile:10|padding_right_mobile:10"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="60" screen_tablet_spacer_size="50" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_family:BebasNeueRegular|letter_spacing:0" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_family:QwigleyRegular" subtitle="Which one is your brief?" heading_margin="margin-bottom:10px;"]Installation Art, Projection Art, or Brand Activation?[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/6"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="2/3"][vc_column_text css=""]Lots of questions come up when you're commissioning a art project . This table sets out a few typical ones, and then details what Oddtoe can achieve.

Installation art Projection art Brand activation
What it is Physical objects built into a space Light and animation thrown onto a surface A branded experience built for a campaign
Where it lives Galleries, foyers, parks, festival grounds Building facades, walls, laneways, interiors Shopping centres, expos, festivals, retail
How long it stays up Weeks to months One night to a season, indoors or after dark Days to a few weeks
Who commissions it Curators, councils, venues, property owners Festivals, councils, precinct associations Marketing and activation agencies, brands
Site requirements Structural mounting, floor space, often power Projector positions, throw distance, darkness Build access, power, and a run schedule
What Oddtoe delivers Concept, 3D design, fabrication, install Concept, animation content, projection Concept, props, fabrication, install, run

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/6"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="60" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="default_row_small_paddings" anchor="who" dfd_row_responsive_enable="dfd-row-responsive-enable" responsive_styles="padding_left_mobile:10|padding_right_mobile:10"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="60" screen_tablet_spacer_size="50" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_family:BebasNeueRegular|letter_spacing:0" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_family:QwigleyRegular" subtitle="Galleries, festivals, venues, and agencies" heading_margin="margin-bottom:10px;"]Who Commissions an Installation Artist?[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4" css=".vc_custom_oddtoe_col_gutter{padding-left: 20px;padding-right: 20px;}"][vc_column_text css=""]The short answer is: Galleries, museums, festivals and local councils; and then there's property owners, event venues, and of course, marketing and activation agencies working for brands. Each wants a different outcome from the same craft: a curated exhibit, a crowd after that comes after dark, a photographed foyer, or a campaign moment.

Australia’s art galleries and museums are a $2.6 billion industry in 2025-26, according to IBISWorld, which notes that institutions are staging immersive and experiential exhibitions that audiences will pay premium prices to see.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4" css=".vc_custom_oddtoe_col_gutter{padding-left: 20px;padding-right: 20px;}"][vc_column_text css=""]Curators and cultural institutions commission work that carries an idea and survives a season of public traffic.

Festivals and councils commission work that pulls people into a laneway, a park, or a main street after dark.

Venues, resorts, and property owners commission a hero piece — the thing in the foyer or the courtyard that guests photograph.

Agencies and brands commission installations as part of an activation. Oddtoe works as the junior partner on those: see experiential marketing.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="default_row_small_paddings" anchor="how" dfd_row_responsive_enable="dfd-row-responsive-enable" responsive_styles="padding_left_mobile:10|padding_right_mobile:10"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="60" screen_tablet_spacer_size="50" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_family:BebasNeueRegular|letter_spacing:0" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_family:QwigleyRegular" subtitle="From site visit to install day" heading_margin="margin-bottom:10px;"]How Does an Oddtoe Installation Get Built?[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4" css=".vc_custom_oddtoe_col_gutter{padding-left: 20px;padding-right: 20px;}"][vc_column_text css=""]Six steps: the brief and the site, concept renders in 3D, a materials and fabrication plan, the build, the install, and documentation. Typical lead time is two to three weeks from brief to install day. Fabrication, projection, animation, and install are handled from one studio, so there is no chasing a prop maker, a content studio, and an AV contractor who have never met.

1. Brief and site. Dimensions, access, power, rigging points, sightlines, and how long the piece needs to stand up.

2. Concept renders. Designed in 3D so the client sees the piece in the actual space before anything is cut or planted.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4" css=".vc_custom_oddtoe_col_gutter{padding-left: 20px;padding-right: 20px;}"][vc_column_text css=""]3. Materials and fabrication plan. What gets made in the studio, what goes to a fabricator, and what the schedule and the budget look like.

4. Build. Working with fabricators and suppliers, with regular progress updates rather than a long silence.

5. Install. On site, on the agreed day, with the crew and the permits sorted.

6. Documentation. Photography and video of the finished piece, which is usually what the client actually circulates afterwards.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="default_row_small_paddings" anchor="words" dfd_row_responsive_enable="dfd-row-responsive-enable" responsive_styles="padding_left_mobile:10|padding_right_mobile:10"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="60" screen_tablet_spacer_size="50" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_family:BebasNeueRegular|letter_spacing:0" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_family:QwigleyRegular" subtitle="The bit of the old interview worth keeping" heading_margin="margin-bottom:10px;"]Why Oddtoe Makes Installation Art[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4" css=".vc_custom_oddtoe_col_gutter{padding-left: 20px;padding-right: 20px;}"][vc_column_text css=""]An installation artist is interested in the viewer and in the location the piece is seen. I’d hate to not have those two things in my creative thinking anyway. I like installations that make the viewer think, or see something differently. My own twist is that I don’t mind messing with the viewer in a cheeky, friendly way.

I haven’t seen much creative cheekiness mixed with state-of-the-art technology. That is what I am after with Oddtoe.

My ingredients are part of what makes the work different. The art world was furious at Anish Kapoor for securing exclusive rights to the deepest black paint ever invented. I understand why he did it. I’d give a kidney for a litre of that stuff. That paint is on my list, along with magnets, projected light, taxidermy, kinetic sculptures, and whatever else catches my fancy.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4" css=".vc_custom_oddtoe_col_gutter{padding-left: 20px;padding-right: 20px;}"][vc_column_text css=""]The perfect client is a gallery owner or a museum curator who thinks in future terms. A lot of what I make has today’s zeitgeist in it, even when that is not obvious on the surface — how artificial intelligence will play with humanity, robots, sustainability. Collectors who see value in the collision of design and technology, too. What Oddtoe makes is not hang-it-on-the-wall-and-forget-it art.

The perfect project would involve the person standing next to it. One idea I am working through in my installation series Botanikus Goiterus is plants that speak to people through elaborately designed translators. The messages are generated by an AI and adapt through the back-and-forth, so more of the person ends up in the plant’s sentences. The working ancestor of that idea was the “Baobab Translator” built for Babbling with Baobabs, a 2.1-metre carved tree that answered the audience through Amazon Alexa.

The genuinely crazy thought is uplifting art. Humorous art. The world can be a bleak place, and the arts celebrate melancholy and stark subjects pretty often. Positive psychology earned a seat at the table in its field. I’d like positive art to do the same.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay=""][vc_column width="1/4"][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/2"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="120" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="100" screen_tablet_spacer_size="80" screen_mobile_spacer_size="80"][vc_column_text item_animation="transition.fadeIn"]

Questions about

Installation art?

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_accordion style="style-3" active_section="1" font_size="18" tab_title_google_fonts="yes" tab_title_custom_fonts="font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:700%20bold%20regular%3A700%3Anormal" icon_size="14"][vc_tta_section title="What does an installation artist actually do?" tab_id="1755300000001-installation-artist-faq-1"][vc_column_text css=""]

An installation artist designs and builds three-dimensional work for a specific location, then installs it there. The job covers the concept, the 3D design, the choice of materials, the build with fabricators, and the install itself. Oddtoe works across topiary, robotics, kinetic sculpture, and projected light.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="What is the difference between installation art and sculpture?" tab_id="1755300000002-installation-artist-faq-2"][vc_column_text css=""]

A sculpture is an object that can be moved and shown almost anywhere. An installation is built around its site, so the room, the lighting, and the path the audience takes are part of the work. Many installations contain sculptures; the installation is the whole arrangement.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="How much does an art installation cost?" tab_id="1755300000003-installation-artist-faq-3"][vc_column_text css=""]

Cost is driven by scale, materials, how much fabrication is needed, site access, power and rigging, and how long the piece stays up. A single indoor object and a multi-piece outdoor commission are very different budgets. Oddtoe quotes each brief individually — send the site details and the dates.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="How long does it take to design and build an installation?" tab_id="1755300000004-installation-artist-faq-4"][vc_column_text css=""]

Two to three weeks from brief to install day for a typical piece. Larger multi-piece commissions run longer, because the schedule is driven by fabrication, permits, and site access. Booking early keeps the build window comfortable.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Can an installation be reused at another site?" tab_id="1755300000005-installation-artist-faq-5"][vc_column_text css=""]

Sometimes. Modular pieces, props, and kinetic elements can be re-rigged for a second site if that is planned into the design from the start. Work built into a specific facade, garden, or room usually cannot move without being redesigned.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Do you work with agencies and producers, or only galleries?" tab_id="1755300000006-installation-artist-faq-6"][vc_column_text css=""]

Both. Oddtoe works with curators and venues on gallery and public work, and with advertising, marketing, and activation agencies on brand installations. For agency briefs the studio handles fabrication, projection, animation, and install under one roof.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Where is Oddtoe based, and where do you install?" tab_id="1755300000007-installation-artist-faq-7"][vc_column_text css=""]

Oddtoe is based in Melbourne, Australia, and works with clients in Los Angeles and Berlin. Installations are delivered in Melbourne and across Australia, with travel quoted up front for interstate and overseas sites.

[vc_row bg_check=”row-background-dark” dfd_bg_style=”image” dfd_bg_image_new=”16054″ dfd_bg_image_repeat=”no-repeat” dfd_image_bg_color=”#232C38″ dfd_bg_image_position=”center center” dfd_overlay_color=”#232C38″ dfd_overlay_pattern=”transperant” dfd_overlay_pattern_opacity=”70″ dfd_row_config=”full_width_content” anchor=”hero”][vc_column]

Installation Artist

[/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check=”row-background-dark”][vc_column]

Sculpture, topiary, robotics, and light in one room

Installation Art & Experiential Design

[vc_column_text css=””]

Updated August 2026

[/vc_column_text]

[vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″ css=”.vc_custom_oddtoe_col_gutter{padding-left: 20px;padding-right: 20px;}”][vc_column_text css=””]Oddtoe is an experiential design and generative-AI animation studio based in Melbourne, creating projection, installation, and animated work for events, venues, and galleries. As an installation artist, I build pieces that occupy a room rather than hang on its wall. Topiary, robotics, kinetic sculpture, and projected light, assembled into one thing an audience can walk around.[/vc_column_text]
[/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″ css=”.vc_custom_oddtoe_col_gutter{padding-left: 20px;padding-right: 20px;}”][vc_column_text]The work is site-specific. A gallery, a hotel foyer, a laneway, a festival field, and a shopping centre atrium all want different objects, so the design starts with the space and the route people take through it. I design in 3D first, then work with fabricators to get the piece built and installed. See the studio’s experiential marketing services or the brand activation ideas list.[/vc_column_text]
[/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner]
[/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check=”row-background-dark” dfd_row_responsive_enable=”dfd-row-responsive-enable” responsive_styles=”padding_left_mobile:10|padding_right_mobile:10″][vc_column]

Installation art, kinetic sculpture, topiary, and projection

Installation Artist & Experiential Designer

[/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row dfd_enable_overlay=”” anchor=”work”][vc_column]
[/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check=”row-background-dark” dfd_enable_overlay=”” dfd_row_config=”default_row_small_paddings” one_page_title=”What?” anchor=”what” dfd_row_parallax=”dfd-row-parallax” dfd_row_responsive_enable=”dfd-row-responsive-enable” responsive_styles=”padding_left_mobile:10|padding_right_mobile:10″][vc_column]

The room is part of the artwork

What Is Installation Art?

[vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″ css=”.vc_custom_oddtoe_col_gutter{padding-left: 20px;padding-right: 20px;}”][vc_column_text css=””]Installation art is three-dimensional work made for a particular space, where the room, the route through it, and the audience are all part of the piece. A painting works on any wall. An installation is designed around its site, its lighting, and the way people move past it.

The term covers a lot of ground. It can be one large object under a spotlight, a whole room the audience walks into, or a set of pieces spread across a park.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″ css=”.vc_custom_oddtoe_col_gutter{padding-left: 20px;padding-right: 20px;}”][vc_column_text css=””]What those have in common is that the location is not a backdrop. Move the work somewhere else and it becomes a different work.

Oddtoe treats that as the interesting part of the job. If a viewer has to walk around something, then their path, their eye line, and what they see when they turn around are all things to design. Closely related practices — kinetic sculpture and projection art — often end up inside the same commission.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner]

[/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check=”row-background-dark” dfd_enable_overlay=”” dfd_row_config=”default_row_small_paddings” dfd_row_responsive_enable=”dfd-row-responsive-enable” responsive_styles=”padding_left_mobile:10|padding_right_mobile:10″][vc_column]

Living material, metal, machinery, and light

What Goes Into an Oddtoe Installation?

[vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″ css=”.vc_custom_oddtoe_col_gutter{padding-left: 20px;padding-right: 20px;}”][vc_column_text css=””]Topiary, robotics, kinetic sculpture, projected light, and generative-AI animation. Most Oddtoe installations combine several of these in one piece — a planted form with a moving mechanical element, projected onto after dark. Materials I’ve used (and wish to use) include living plants, sheet metal, resin, and fired clay.

Each of those is a practice in its own right, and each has its own page:[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″ css=”.vc_custom_oddtoe_col_gutter{padding-left: 20px;padding-right: 20px;}”][vc_column_text css=””]• Topiary and planted forms
• Kinetic sculpture
• Robotics and animatronics
• Projection and light
• Props and fabricated objects
• Sensory garden design
• Giant inflatables and walk-in structures

The newer ingredient is generative AI, used for concept exploration and for the animated content that gets projected onto a built piece. There is a full explainer on what generative AI animation is.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner]

[/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check=”row-background-dark” dfd_enable_overlay=”” dfd_row_responsive_enable=”dfd-row-responsive-enable” responsive_styles=”padding_left_mobile:10|padding_right_mobile:10″][vc_column]

Which one is your brief?

Installation Art, Projection Art, or Brand Activation?

[vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/6″][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”2/3″][vc_column_text css=””]Lots of questions come up when you’re commissioning a art project . This table sets out a few typical ones, and then details what Oddtoe can achieve.

Installation art Projection art Brand activation
What it is Physical objects built into a space Light and animation thrown onto a surface A branded experience built for a campaign
Where it lives Galleries, foyers, parks, festival grounds Building facades, walls, laneways, interiors Shopping centres, expos, festivals, retail
How long it stays up Weeks to months One night to a season, indoors or after dark Days to a few weeks
Who commissions it Curators, councils, venues, property owners Festivals, councils, precinct associations Marketing and activation agencies, brands
Site requirements Structural mounting, floor space, often power Projector positions, throw distance, darkness Build access, power, and a run schedule
What Oddtoe delivers Concept, 3D design, fabrication, install Concept, animation content, projection Concept, props, fabrication, install, run

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/6″][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner]

[/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check=”row-background-dark” dfd_enable_overlay=”” dfd_row_config=”default_row_small_paddings” anchor=”who” dfd_row_responsive_enable=”dfd-row-responsive-enable” responsive_styles=”padding_left_mobile:10|padding_right_mobile:10″][vc_column]

Galleries, festivals, venues, and agencies

Who Commissions an Installation Artist?

[vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″ css=”.vc_custom_oddtoe_col_gutter{padding-left: 20px;padding-right: 20px;}”][vc_column_text css=””]The short answer is: Galleries, museums, festivals and local councils; and then there’s property owners, event venues, and of course, marketing and activation agencies working for brands. Each wants a different outcome from the same craft: a curated exhibit, a crowd after that comes after dark, a photographed foyer, or a campaign moment.

Australia’s art galleries and museums are a $2.6 billion industry in 2025-26, according to IBISWorld, which notes that institutions are staging immersive and experiential exhibitions that audiences will pay premium prices to see.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″ css=”.vc_custom_oddtoe_col_gutter{padding-left: 20px;padding-right: 20px;}”][vc_column_text css=””]Curators and cultural institutions commission work that carries an idea and survives a season of public traffic.

Festivals and councils commission work that pulls people into a laneway, a park, or a main street after dark.

Venues, resorts, and property owners commission a hero piece — the thing in the foyer or the courtyard that guests photograph.

Agencies and brands commission installations as part of an activation. Oddtoe works as the junior partner on those: see experiential marketing.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner]

[/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check=”row-background-dark” dfd_enable_overlay=”” dfd_row_config=”default_row_small_paddings” anchor=”how” dfd_row_responsive_enable=”dfd-row-responsive-enable” responsive_styles=”padding_left_mobile:10|padding_right_mobile:10″][vc_column]

From site visit to install day

How Does an Oddtoe Installation Get Built?

[vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″ css=”.vc_custom_oddtoe_col_gutter{padding-left: 20px;padding-right: 20px;}”][vc_column_text css=””]Six steps: the brief and the site, concept renders in 3D, a materials and fabrication plan, the build, the install, and documentation. Typical lead time is two to three weeks from brief to install day. Fabrication, projection, animation, and install are handled from one studio, so there is no chasing a prop maker, a content studio, and an AV contractor who have never met.

1. Brief and site. Dimensions, access, power, rigging points, sightlines, and how long the piece needs to stand up.

2. Concept renders. Designed in 3D so the client sees the piece in the actual space before anything is cut or planted.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″ css=”.vc_custom_oddtoe_col_gutter{padding-left: 20px;padding-right: 20px;}”][vc_column_text css=””]3. Materials and fabrication plan. What gets made in the studio, what goes to a fabricator, and what the schedule and the budget look like.

4. Build. Working with fabricators and suppliers, with regular progress updates rather than a long silence.

5. Install. On site, on the agreed day, with the crew and the permits sorted.

6. Documentation. Photography and video of the finished piece, which is usually what the client actually circulates afterwards.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner]

[/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check=”row-background-dark” dfd_enable_overlay=”” dfd_row_config=”default_row_small_paddings” anchor=”words” dfd_row_responsive_enable=”dfd-row-responsive-enable” responsive_styles=”padding_left_mobile:10|padding_right_mobile:10″][vc_column]

The bit of the old interview worth keeping

Why Oddtoe Makes Installation Art

[vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″ css=”.vc_custom_oddtoe_col_gutter{padding-left: 20px;padding-right: 20px;}”][vc_column_text css=””]An installation artist is interested in the viewer and in the location the piece is seen. I’d hate to not have those two things in my creative thinking anyway. I like installations that make the viewer think, or see something differently. My own twist is that I don’t mind messing with the viewer in a cheeky, friendly way.

I haven’t seen much creative cheekiness mixed with state-of-the-art technology. That is what I am after with Oddtoe.

My ingredients are part of what makes the work different. The art world was furious at Anish Kapoor for securing exclusive rights to the deepest black paint ever invented. I understand why he did it. I’d give a kidney for a litre of that stuff. That paint is on my list, along with magnets, projected light, taxidermy, kinetic sculptures, and whatever else catches my fancy.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″ css=”.vc_custom_oddtoe_col_gutter{padding-left: 20px;padding-right: 20px;}”][vc_column_text css=””]The perfect client is a gallery owner or a museum curator who thinks in future terms. A lot of what I make has today’s zeitgeist in it, even when that is not obvious on the surface — how artificial intelligence will play with humanity, robots, sustainability. Collectors who see value in the collision of design and technology, too. What Oddtoe makes is not hang-it-on-the-wall-and-forget-it art.

The perfect project would involve the person standing next to it. One idea I am working through in my installation series Botanikus Goiterus is plants that speak to people through elaborately designed translators. The messages are generated by an AI and adapt through the back-and-forth, so more of the person ends up in the plant’s sentences. The working ancestor of that idea was the “Baobab Translator” built for Babbling with Baobabs, a 2.1-metre carved tree that answered the audience through Amazon Alexa.

The genuinely crazy thought is uplifting art. Humorous art. The world can be a bleak place, and the arts celebrate melancholy and stark subjects pretty often. Positive psychology earned a seat at the table in its field. I’d like positive art to do the same.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/4″][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner]

[/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check=”row-background-dark” dfd_enable_overlay=””][vc_column width=”1/4″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/2″]

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title=”Where is Oddtoe based, and where do you install?” tab_id=”1755300000007-installation-artist-faq-7″][vc_column_text css=””]

Oddtoe is based in Melbourne, Australia, and works with clients in Los Angeles and Berlin. Installations are delivered in Melbourne and across Australia, with travel quoted up front for interstate and overseas sites.
